content.text:
Fixed. All 1633 tests pass and lint shows only pre-existing warnings.

**Cause.** In `lib/parse.js`, the numeric-entity step ran `String(val)` on the parsed value. When `comma: true` had already split the value into an array, that call joined it back into a single comma-separated string, so the split was lost.

**Fix.** The entity interpretation now maps over the value with the existing `utils.maybeMap` helper, so each array element is decoded individually and strings are handled as before.

**Tests.** In `test/parse.js` I added a regression test covering the reported case, entity interpretation inside split values, a single value without commas, and unchanged utf-8 behaviour. One existing test had asserted the old collapsed output for `a[]=1,☺`. I updated it to expect the nested-array shape, which is what the same input already produces under utf-8.
